dedupe_keys.name: microsoft azure status history and post incident reviews pirs

description: The Azure status history page is Microsoft's public archive of Post Incident Reviews (PIRs) for Azure service issues. Since 20 November 2019 Microsoft has published a PIR for every issue it communicated publicly, and from 1 June 2022 the scope was widened; each review is kept for five years. Microsoft aims to post a preliminary review within three days of mitigation and a final one after its internal retrospective, usually within 14 days. Each PIR sets out what happened, the root cause, how Microsoft responded with a timeline, what it is changing and advice to customers, and many are accompanied by recorded incident retrospective videos. Examples include cooling and power failures in individual data centres, such as the 2023 Australia East cooling outage, and network connectivity incidents such as one affecting West US in July 2026. The page can be filtered by date range, product and region. Coverage: Azure regions worldwide, 2019 onward on a five-year rolling basis. Format and access: web pages, free to read. Caveats: rolling retention means older reviews disappear; reviews are written by the provider and are not structured data. Simulation uses: failure and recovery timelines for data-centre and cloud dependency models, root-cause statistics for risk assessment and scenario design. Related records: the Azure Australia East cooling outage case study draws on one PIR, and AWS and Google Cloud publish comparable archives.
